overview: 40 official Group 1 Prelims questions (2008–2024): ISRO missions and launchers (16 Qs) and DRDO missiles/defence tech (15 Qs) carry the section; satellites (communication, NavIC, remote sensing, defence, student) add 8. Up to 2019 mostly one-liners (missile type, range, satellite purpose); 2023–24 turned to 3–4-statement sets on Gaganyaan, SSLV, Vikram-S, Mission Shakti, WESAT, where one number, vehicle or developer is swapped.

possibility.angle: Evolution of Indian space programme, private space sector
possibility.evidence: 1 Q: 2023 (Vikram-S); related exams ask SITE 1975, Aryabhata launch site
possibility.what_they_ask: first privately built rocket and its developer, mission name, early milestones (Thumba, Aryabhata 1975, SITE)

possibility.angle: ISRO missions and launch vehicles (Chandrayaan, Gaganyaan, SSLV, GSLV Mk III)
possibility.what_they_ask: mission target and type (lunar probe, Venus orbiter), launcher for a mission, SSLV/GSLV specifications, astronaut names, foreign satellites on PSLV, space-medicine terms
period of a geostationary satellite, launch date, NSIL-owned GSAT and why a foreign rocket
which country owns which GNSS (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, NavIC), atomic clocks in space

possibility.evidence: 1 Q: 2019 (ScatSat); related exams ask NRSC Hyderabad, IIRS Dehradun
possibility.what_they_ask: purpose of a named satellite (ScatSat = weather/ocean winds), location of NRSC/IIRS

possibility.evidence: 1 Q: 2024 (spy satellite built by Tata Advanced Systems)
possibility.what_they_ask: which company built a military satellite, which rocket carries it; GSAT-7 series, EMISAT, RISAT are natural next targets
which college built it, which mission carried it, what it measures; EDUSAT 2004 as the education satellite

missile class (Nag anti-tank, BrahMos anti-ship, anti-radiation), range (Agni-I, Agni-III), submarine launch (Sagarika), UAV/torpedo names (TAPAS, Varunastra), Mission Shakti facts, PSU that makes missiles (BDL)

traps.trap: [E20/1] Right rocket, rival startup as developer
traps.spot: private launch vehicle statement naming a startup
traps.fix: Skyroot (Hyderabad) → Vikram-S, mission Prarambh 2022; Agnikul (Chennai) → Agnibaan
traps.pyq: 'Vikram-S … developed by Agnikul Cosmos' → Skyroot Aerospace [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#108]

traps.trap: Launcher downgraded to an older vehicle
traps.spot: 'planned to be launched on GSLV Mk II' for a heavy/crewed mission
traps.fix: Gaganyaan flies on human-rated LVM3 (ex-GSLV Mk III); Mk II is too small

traps.spot: a descriptive word about a named robot or person
traps.fix: Vyommitra is a female half-humanoid robot

traps.spot: technical specs of a launcher with round numbers
traps.fix: SSLV = 3 solid stages + liquid VTM, ~120 t, 34 m, 500 kg to 500 km
traps.pyq: 'two solid motor stages … 100 tonnes' → three stages, ~120 t [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#77]

traps.spot: 'done in the upper atmosphere to ensure no debris'
traps.fix: Low altitude (~283 km) was chosen so debris decays quickly – lower, not upper

traps.spot: options list anti-tank, anti-ship, SAM, SSM for one name
traps.fix: Nag = anti-tank (fire-and-forget); BrahMos = supersonic cruise, anti-ship; Akash/Trishul = SAM; Prithvi/Agni = ballistic

traps.trap: Owner country swapped in a GNSS pair
traps.fix: GLONASS = Russia; Galileo = EU; BeiDou = China; NavIC = India

traps.spot: a student/small satellite paired with an earth-science objective
traps.fix: WESAT measures solar UV radiation; it is not a groundwater mission
traps.pyq: 'WESAT … rainfall refills underground water' → solar UV [group1-prelims-2024-paper2#63]

traps.spot: a list of 5 names when the real set is 4
traps.fix: Gaganyaan four: P. Balakrishnan Nair, Ajit Krishnan, Angad Pratap, Shubhanshu Shukla
traps.pyq: 'Gp Capt Pankaj M. Sinha' → not selected [group1-prelims-2024-paper2#102]

techniques.name: [E20/8] Name-to-class decoding
techniques.how: Recall the missile/system family by name (Agni/Prithvi ballistic, Akash/Trishul SAM, Nag/Helina anti-tank, Varunastra torpedo); strike options of other classes.
techniques.example: 'Fire and Forget anti-tank' → Agni (ballistic), Akash and Trishul (SAM) fall → Nag [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#68]

techniques.name: Spec-sheet audit
techniques.how: For launcher/mission statements, check each number (stages, mass, payload, altitude) against the vehicle's spec card; one wrong number sinks the statement.
techniques.example: SSLV: 500 kg/500 km true, shorter than PSLV true, vertical+horizontal assembly true, 'two stages/100 t' false → I, III and IV only [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#77]

techniques.name: Physics anchor for orbits
techniques.how: Use the defining property instead of memory: geostationary = same rotation period as Earth.
techniques.example: Geostationary period → 365 days, 30 days, 12 hours fall → 1 day [group1-prelims-2010#122]

techniques.name: Codes elimination from one sure statement
techniques.how: Find the statement you are surest about, strike codes that contradict it, then test only what still differs.
techniques.example: Vikram-S developer is Skyroot → IV false → only 'I, II and III only' survives [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#108]

techniques.name: Count-the-set
techniques.how: When you know how many genuine items exist, find the extra one; every code with it falls.
techniques.example: Four Gaganyaan astronauts; Pankaj Sinha is the extra → codes with III fall → I, II, IV and V [group1-prelims-2024-paper2#102]

techniques.name: Purpose-from-name
techniques.how: Read the satellite/system name for its mission (Scat = scatterometer, Nav = navigation, Edu = education), then match.
techniques.example: ScatSat carries a scatterometer for ocean winds → weather monitoring [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#75]

confusions.remember: Vikram-S (Hyderabad) 2022 first private rocket; Agnibaan (Chennai) semi-cryogenic, 2024
Heavy and crewed missions (Chandrayaan-2/3, Gaganyaan) use LVM3
SSLV 3 solid stages + VTM, 34 m; PSLV 4 stages (solid-liquid alternating), 44 m
Nag = anti-tank; BrahMos = India–Russia supersonic cruise, anti-ship
Sagarika (K-15) = submarine-launched (2008 test); Dhanush = ship-launched Prithvi
BDL makes guided missiles; BEL makes defence electronics/radars
WESAT = student solar-UV payload; XPoSat = primary X-ray polarimetry satellite, both PSLV-C58
TAPAS = medium-altitude long-endurance; NETRA = mini UAV / AEW&C; Nishant = tactical UAV
Anti-radiation homes on enemy radar emissions (e.g. Rudram)

anchors: 27 March 2019 – Mission Shakti: DRDO PDV Mk-II destroyed Microsat-R (~283 km); India 4th after US, Russia, China
SSLV – 500 kg to 500 km, 3 solid stages + VTM, ~120 t
Gaganyaan – HLVM3; Vyommitra female robot; DRDO human-centric systems; 4 astronaut-designates (27 Feb 2024)
Sagarika – first underwater (submarine-launched) missile test, 26 Feb 2008
Ammonium perchlorate – oxidiser in solid rocket fuel
GSLV Mk III-D1 – 'game changer' heavy launcher (2017)
Sriharikota (Nellore district) – SDSC SHAR; visitor gallery capacity 5,000
WESAT – LBS Institute of Technology for Women, Thiruvananthapuram; PSLV-C58, 1 Jan 2024
checklist: Which family is the name from – ISRO vehicle, DRDO missile, private startup?
Check every number (stages, tonnes, km, year) against the spec card.
Developer statements: verify the company/lab, not just the product.
In name lists, count the genuine set and find the extra.
Mind the date of the news: 'scheduled' claims age quickly.
